workflow.title: Separate duplicate files from rebuildable caches before a Mac cleanup
workflow.primaryIntent: Choose the appropriate review queue for duplicates, app leftovers and caches rather than deleting by size alone.
workflow.lead: Use separate review steps for duplicate candidates, app leftovers and rebuildable caches. MacCleaner Pro documents separate tools for these jobs; a storage total alone is not permission to delete.
outline: Inventory first; keep originals and backups out of automatic decisions
Map duplicate/folder review to the suite's Duplicate File Finder, app removal to App Cleaner & Uninstaller, and caches to its cleaner
Explain that duplicate-looking content is not necessarily disposable; no automatic deletion instructions
Contrast a one-time sorting job with investigating recurring growth, without asserting the competitor lacks monitoring
Give a bounded choice: suite for documented duplicate/uninstall jobs, Breathing Room source preview for investigation with release and hosted caveats
workflow.distinctness: Suite-specific multi-tool triage workflow, not a reworded generic cleaner comparison or an App Cleaner uninstall tutorial.
workflow.visualPlan: Cleared competitor app UI immediately after lead; later labeled Breathing Room Space preview. Currently blocked, do not replace competitor image with logo or generated UI.
workflow.interactionPass: Draft-stage decision checklist: identify item type, confirm ownership/backup, estimate rebuild/download cost, inspect proposed action. No filesystem access, upload, deletions or fabricated savings.
workflow.evidenceBoundaries: Planning brief only, not a tested tutorial. Do not invent button paths, duplicate-matching algorithms, Trash handling or measured performance. No FAQ unless real questions are sourced.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs MacCleaner Pro: investigation or cleanup toolkit?
